key_insight: CARDIAC-FM is a multimodal foundation model that learns shared cardiac signals from ECG and cardiac MRI to improve generalizable cardiovascular risk prediction.
clinical_relevance: It may help identify people at higher risk of atrial fibrillation, heart failure, and other cardiovascular outcomes more accurately than ECG-only AI models, especially when combined with standard clinical risk scores.
method: Self-supervised learning on paired 12-lead ECG and cardiac MRI data
Cross-modal contrastive alignment between ECG and MRI representations
Spatiotemporal, multi-view masked autoencoding for cardiac MRI
evidence_signal: The model was developed on 57,609 paired ECG-MRI samples from UK Biobank and showed improved prediction plus zero-shot generalization to the Cardiovascular Health Study and the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis.
watch_item: External performance and real-world deployment still need validation across diverse imaging protocols, populations, and clinical workflows.
paper_title: CARDIAC-FM: A Generalizable Multimodal Foundation Model Integrating ECG and Cardiac MRI
